_comment: #571/#512 continuous fresh caster history, title to epilogue. Mage is the first class (Pisces's actual lesson), evolves to Ice Mage at sleep and ends Ice Mage 14; Rogue/Diplomat/Archer/Trader are incidental or social support (drainage crossing, crate and alley rewards, drayman/gossip, purchases). Every fight is player-driven: number-key or clicked bar casts, Frost Bolt/Ice Shard/Calming Touch, no combat_autoplay. Two carried fights in one waking (road, then the optional sewer bats at 0 MP); sleeps refill to the new maxima. Four Xif Mana Potions bought for real: two drunk in the warden fight at 1 AP each, then doses 3 (safe) and 4 (warning, Cancel, accepted -4 HP) outside combat, then a pause-menu Save/Load. No fixtures, teleports, top-ups, retries or farming; ledger in docs/design/571-ledger-caster.md.

A Watch runner is looking for you.

There you are. The cisterns crew found something under the new grates: tunnels nobody dug, going down past where their lanterns reached. Olesm's maps say they shouldn't exist. You've been down there. You're going again, this time for the Watch.

payload_contains.speaker: Zevara

You lower yourself into the fissure. The sewer's damp falls away behind you, and a dry, ancient cold rises to meet your hands. The dark below swallows the last of the light from above.
A pit at the middle of the stone ring, the ash dead to the bottom. Bones banked against the stones, every one opened for the marrow.

Cracked bones in a heap, dry and light in the hand. Most of them Gnoll; one a Drake's.
The tunnel widens into a pillared gallery, the air stirring with breath that is not your own. Something large shifts in the dark ahead, and the pacing scuffs go quiet. You have found the warren.

payload_contains.speaker: Olesm
payload_contains.text: The Watch wants eyes on the reopened gallery — proper eyes. The last guardsman down there filed three words: 'it is dark.' Five gold now, fifteen when you bring me something I can put in a report. The Guild is sending a Silver-rank team to meet you there.
The gallery floor slopes down past where the den used to be. You come out in the delve's staging chamber.

payload_contains.speaker: Ceria
payload_contains.text: Rules are simple. Traps kill more adventurers than monsters do, so nobody touches anything shiny. See something worth grabbing, you call me over and you wait.

payload_contains.speaker: Ceria
payload_contains.text: All right. Four of us on the roster, three of us actually walking in — Pisces bills from a distance. Try to keep up.

payload_contains.speaker: Ksmvr
payload_contains.text: I understand. I will step only where you have said. If I am wrong, I apologize in advance.

payload_contains.speaker: Ksmvr
payload_contains.text: I did not die. This is the preferred outcome.
The runes are the same. The same hand, the same order, as the door in the inn's pantry.
The rubble gives at your push; the path through it was cleared before you got here. The old gallery beyond is dark, but it is open.

payload_contains.speaker: Olesm
payload_contains.text: A construct. A vault. Another rune-door — another. Do you know what this does to my casualty projections? Nothing good. Here is your fifteen. Earned.

payload_contains.speaker: Ceria
payload_contains.text: It was guarding a door. Wonderful. Somebody left a construct in the dark to watch one door, and we still don't know what's on the other side.

payload_contains.speaker: Ceria
payload_contains.text: Word travels. Yes — there's a ruin out past the floodplains, and under it a level nobody's opened since before Liscor had walls. We hit the seal three days ago. Yvlon can't cut it, and the one mage in this city who could read it works for himself and charges accordingly. We need one more pair of hands.

payload_contains.speaker: Ceria
payload_contains.text: If I knew, I wouldn't need a dig. Whatever it is, someone sealed it on purpose and did a very good job. Usually that means valuable or it means dangerous. I plan the camp for dangerous.

payload_contains.speaker: Ceria
payload_contains.text: East past the gate road, across the floodplains — follow the survey stakes. Ask for me at the camp. And bring your own rope.
[Mage Level 8 → 10] (+1 Max MP) — sleep restores HP and MP.
[Rogue Level 3] — unlocked [Find Trap]
[Mage] has become [Ice Mage]!
The seam splits wider at your touch, cold air breathing out of the dark beneath. You step through, into somewhere else.
East past the gate road, across the floodplains — this is the ruin. Survey stakes, a banked fire, washing on a line: the Horns got here first. The sealed level is deeper in, under the pedestal court.

payload_contains.speaker: Ceria
payload_contains.text: You made it. Camp rules: nobody touches anything shiny, nobody wanders past the survey stakes alone. The sealed level's below the pedestal court. We found the site off an old expedition ledger — half the pages are about what they didn't bring out. It's in my tent, filed with the survey maps.

The seal is broken and the Horns are already down the gap — Yvlon bracing, Ksmvr counting rope. The warding still holds the stone fast. Two spiral plates flank the court; Ceria points at the carving beside the pedestal and says that one's a beginning.

Below the pedestal: not treasure. A door, unhung, unmarked, utterly ordinary except that four adventurers go silent around it at once. Ceria, finally: 'That's wardwork. Old, fed wardwork. We're taking it home.' The anchor stone comes up with it.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: Mounted and hinged. Observe — already holding a hop to Liscor's gate district, and nobody has offered it so much as a rune of encouragement. It works. The next test is range.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: Farther than Liscor. The wardwork is straining for distance; set a palm to the frame and you can feel the pull. But push it unattuned and things we did not invite will leak through. So we attune it properly. Krshia stocks the catalysts, and I have already started on the calculations for our half of the work.
Cold light, gone as fast as it came. The gate district's noise rushes back in around you.

payload_contains.speaker: Zevara
payload_contains.text: Good. The Watch posts standing bounties on anything that made a file cross my desk. You clear it and claim it here. I sign it. Keep the receipts honest. The Council audits the ledger every month.

payload_contains.speaker: Zevara
payload_contains.text: Signed. Mind the ink, it's still wet.

payload_contains.speaker: Krshia
payload_contains.text: Silverfang goods. Best in Liscor, and I will hear no argument on it. Cheapest at the front, the good stock where a browsing hand drifts. Coin on the counter and it is yours. No discounts, no haggling. I remember faces.

payload_contains.speaker: Krshia
payload_contains.text: The charmed stock costs more because it does more. Wear too much of it at once and it starts to argue with itself, so choose with sense. Coin on the counter, same as the rest.

payload_contains.speaker: Krshia
payload_contains.text: That one, I do not ask questions about. Silverfang trade brings stranger things than that through Liscor. It came in under the wool two winters back and it has sat under that cloth since. Yours now. Wrap it before you carry it. It hums against tin, yes?

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: A door that changes its mind about where it goes. How very like this city — even the fixtures have moods. You could bleed for my curiosity, if that is your instrument. You could attempt to talk me into caring, which has been done, rarely. Or prove you can read a ward without my help, and I will be forced to take you seriously. Choose, and do not waste my morning.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: You want me to walk into someone's pantry and grope at a wild ward with my bare senses. No. I have wards of my own I would rather keep.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: A glance. Hm. If it truly reads as spatial and not necrotic, I could examine it without touching a thing. Fine — for the intellectual insult of not knowing. Do not mistake this for a favor.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: A spatial anchor. Crude. Fascinating. Whoever built your inn, adventurer, built it on something that remembers being elsewhere.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: Then the scholarship is done and the tedium begins. Keep both near the door, and rest. Rest is the instruction; I am aware of how it sounds. Attunement is a residency — the frame learns the stone the way a house learns its family: overnight, and more than once. Sleep. Let the inn do the part no [Mage] can rush.
Your own bed.
Your own bed.
Your own bed.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: The same hand, then, on both sides of the city. Two workings, one wardwright, and no version of that I can make boring. I should very much like to read that wardwork myself — after you have slept. My notes on our frame want reorganizing before I stand in front of its sibling.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: The Door will show you how far it wants to go. And somewhere under this city is wardwork by the same hand, still fed, still waiting. I intend to understand both. Go — see where it reaches.
The light warms and the air smells of wheat and river water before you've taken a step. Riverfarm, same as the rumor said.

payload_contains.speaker: A Shepherd
payload_contains.text: Stand the watch with me and we thin them. Or the hurdles are cut for a new fold. That's the two I've got. Wolves don't move ground for nothing.
You walk the sign back. The pack came off the north ground by the old line — something denned in it and they gave way. They didn't choose these fields. They were pushed.

payload_contains.speaker: Eloise
payload_contains.text: There's no blight. Someone in that village struck a bargain with me — asked a favor, got exactly what they asked for. The price was always the second half of the deal, and they're pretending they forgot that part. The craft has been collecting on the debt ever since, out of their fields.

payload_contains.speaker: Eloise
payload_contains.text: Broker. That's a word for it. Go on, then, make your pitch. I'll hear it out. I've settled for less than I was owed before now.

payload_contains.speaker: Eloise
payload_contains.text: A year, tending my hearth. Wood in winter, the kettle seen to the year round. It falls short of the debt I was owed. It might do.

payload_contains.speaker: Eloise
payload_contains.text: Fine. Tea first, and then it's settled. A year's honest work from a village that never meant to keep its favor. The woodpile is behind the house; tell them it starts there.

payload_contains.speaker: Eloise
payload_contains.text: Coin, then. Fine — not everyone wants to owe me something bigger. Take what you need and go.
The stone is warm and it keeps turning a little north in your hand. Ask the Door for Invrisil now and it will know what you mean.

payload_contains.speaker: Eloise
payload_contains.text: That stone's walked the Invrisil road more times than I have. Keep it in a dry pocket, on the side you don't fall on. Don't lose it before you get there.

payload_contains.speaker: Former Headman
payload_contains.text: Handled. Good. I won't ask how. Whatever you did, thank you. Truly. Now there's hay down and rain coming, so I'd best be at it.

payload_contains.speaker: A Shepherd
payload_contains.text: Pushed. Off their own ground, by the old line. So it was never my fields they wanted. Wolves and me both, working round something neither of us can see.
You take a scrap off its hook and spend the morning behind it. Ditching, mostly. The pay is small coin, counted out the same day.

payload_contains.speaker: Eloise
payload_contains.text: Your door smells of a feeding ward. I keep one myself — smaller. Sit. If you're going to live over one, you'll learn what it eats.

payload_contains.speaker: Eloise
payload_contains.text: Mine takes milk and a word, every seventh night. Yours was built to hold something that argues back, and a ward like that gets fed on purpose, by someone who meant it to outlast them. Don't starve it in a hurry, child. Left hungry, it will start drawing what it needs from whatever is nearest — the heat off your hearth first, then the sleep of whoever lives over it.
The light turns pale and cool, and the noise of a much bigger city rushes in to fill the silence. Invrisil, same as the letter promised.

The stacks against this wall wear the same burgundy brand as the frontage up the square. Out there, COYLE AND SONS keeps one modest door; back here the wagons idle and the men loading them count every crate twice.

payload_contains.speaker: Cups
payload_contains.text: Here's the third thing, then, since you keep buying the first two. I owe the Brothers a debt I've been quietly not paying. A chit, is all. But it's got Wilovan's own mark on it, and I'd rather it went back quiet, with you, before anyone's sent to collect it. Carry it to the parlor, quiet as you came by it, and we'll talk about faces.

payload_contains.speaker: Cups
payload_contains.text: Free tea, then. You'd be surprised how few take just the tea. Sit, drink it while it's hot. Crate's still wobbly — sit to the left and it won't tip.
Whatever was watching that stretch never saw you pass.
Whatever was watching that stretch never saw you pass.
Whatever was watching that stretch never saw you pass.
Whatever was watching that stretch never saw you pass.

steps._comment: Flash Step (Mage 11) pushed [Calming Touch] to bar slot 10, past the number keys: clicked.

payload_contains.speaker: Cups
payload_contains.text: Every hat, hm. You know what nobody's ever offered the tea-girl before? Standing. Done. Pour it in ink, I'll sign. But one cup won't drown a man like Coyle — you want Hellam's grudge on paper next to mine. Come back and say 'pour for three' and I'll have him here, wedding manners and all.

payload_contains.speaker: Cups
payload_contains.text: Done and done. Hellam didn't even finish his cup. Signed and sanded before it cooled. Sealed it himself, then asked could he sign twice. Take the papers wherever names like Coyle's go to be spent. And friend — my own name's in the middle of this one. First time for that. The pot's gone cold.

payload_contains.speaker: Master Coyle
payload_contains.text: Do you know what reputation costs in this city? More than you. Considerably more than him. Whoever sold you that story priced your discretion like an amateur and never thought to price mine at all. So. Prove it, or price your next words very carefully.

payload_contains.speaker: Master Coyle
payload_contains.text: That was a better hand than I priced you for. Sit down. Please. Let us speak as adults who know what things cost. Yes — I paid for the removal; the frame was simply cheaper than the fee. Farley's sort are priced by the dozen — warehouse math, a line in anyone's book. My price would want the city's own books, all of them, and several years of them. So. Name yours. Everyone has one, and today I am buying above market.

payload_contains.speaker: Hedault
payload_contains.text: Hold still. There is a residue on your sleeve I do not see twice in a decade. Ruin warding. A set ward would have gone quiet years ago; this one is fed, and the draw is live. Looking costs nothing.

payload_contains.speaker: Wilovan
payload_contains.text: Then here are the manners of it. You don't name the thing and you don't name the man. Hat stays on, sir, door to door, and the room will read it. Ah — and you don't hurry. A man nearly forgot the one that matters most.
Your hat goes onto the third peg, brim out — nine hats on the rail now; across the room a man lowers his cup an inch and holds it there, watching you.
Your coat goes over the chair back with the package folded into it, beside the one already hanging, and the other coat is over your arm two steps from the door.

payload_contains.speaker: Wilovan
payload_contains.text: It is, sir, and I had it from a man I pay to be certain. Tell me how the room took it, and I'll know what I owe you.

payload_contains.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box

payload_contains.text: My mother's. The stone in it is glass. I have known since I was nineteen and I have never once said so out loud, and I am not going to begin by saying it to a jeweller who will write it on an order. This city is run from a house you cannot see from any street in it, by a woman who notices everything worth noticing. A glass stone is exactly the right size to stay beneath that notice. I intend to keep it there.

Because she wore it to every hard thing she ever did and it never once let her down. The stone was glass for all forty of those years. It did not matter then and I will not let it start mattering now. I want the setting held properly. The stone can stay glass.

There is an enchanter with a bench in the alleys who will not touch a piece until somebody in the transaction tells him the truth about it. He is right to insist and I cannot be the one who does it. Twenty five gold when it is set. Do not be charming at him. My house is down to two assets. The name is one. The other is the habit people have of not looking past it. Tell him the truth of the stone and keep the name out of his order book.

Set it on the cloth. Do not hand it to me. I have looked at it twice already and I will not cut a mount until somebody in this transaction says the true thing out loud: that stone is glass, cut well, sold badly, and about forty years old. I will not cut a mount over a lie. It is half-drawn on the bench behind me, and it stays half-drawn until I hear it.

Good. Then it goes on the order in those words and the price changes, downward, because glass takes less holding than a stone does. Glass wants a shallower seat and a thinner ward-line, which is fewer hours and less silver on my side of the cloth. The mount behind me can be finished this afternoon. I would rather be told than discover it at the bench.

Then it is done, and done in the open, which I did not expect and did not know I wanted. Here. My mother had a second piece, plain, honest, worth a tenth of the first and worn twice as often. I would rather it went to somebody who earned it. It has spent long enough in the box.
It came to my rooms before breakfast. Cream, no crest on it, one line, in a hand I have seen twice in my life on paper I was not supposed to be holding either time. It asks me to confirm a signature.

I have signed nothing of consequence since the year my mother died. I am not going to say whose hand it is in a shop with a scribe in it. You already know which house I mean, because I told you where this city is run from and you did not laugh at me. She does not write to people like me. She writes about them, and only once something with her attention on it has started to move.

Somebody has, and it has been out in this city doing business without me for long enough that a woman who notices everything has seen it. I will not answer that card until I can say who. Start at the counter of this very shop. There is a scribe there who rents a blank seal by the hour and who has never once asked me how I am.
That is my— you are looking at my blotter. People do not look at my blotter.
It is a blotter. It blots. If a man reads it and walks west past the tea and finds a table there, I never said a word to him. Remember it that way.

payload_contains.speaker: A Man with a Rented Table

payload_contains.text: I cut blocks. A block is brass. What a man presses it into is between him and whoever reads the letter. That house has had nothing behind it since before I was born. The initials sat unused all that while, so I cut a block and I have rented it out since. Nobody living had a better claim, that I could find.
A card. To her. Cream, was it, and one line on it? I remember the stock. I did wonder at the time how far the paper would travel. Then the next customer sat down and I had a cut to price.

payload_contains.speaker: A Man with a Rented Table

payload_contains.text: He puts the brass in your hand and keeps his own hand out a moment longer, as if the table might want it back.

payload_contains.speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage

payload_contains.text: Good. Then he was selling it, and nobody had to take it from him, and the lady kept enough of the name to be worth the theft. That will go back exactly as you said it and not one word further. She is paid for her trouble and you are paid for yours. My mistress does not do favours. She does accounts, and she settles them the same week.
Thirty gold, counted out flat on the table with no purse and no flourish, by a woman who has plainly never once had to check the count.

payload_contains.speaker: Selys
payload_contains.text: One job. I flagged it because the client isn't insane and the pay is honest: a courier run out to Riverfarm, nothing that bites back. Bring me the receipt. You get squared from the Guild's own purse, and the client's excuse for one never comes into it.

payload_contains.speaker: Selys
payload_contains.text: Pallass. Guild's got the standing arrangement. I file the sponsorship, you cover the clerk's fee — fee first, actually. It goes through same-day. Ten gold, paid to the Guild, not to me.

payload_contains.speaker: Selys
payload_contains.text: Filed and stamped — same-day, like I said. The Door will answer for Pallass the next time you ask it. That arrangement took the Guild years.

payload_contains.speaker: Krshia
payload_contains.text: Let me see what you're carrying.

steps._comment: Sell list row 0 is the still-held Mending Draught; row 1 is the vault Tonic.

payload_contains.speaker: Krshia
payload_contains.text: Half its worth, paid straight — I don't forget a fair trade any more than an unfair one. Sold.

payload_contains.speaker: Krshia
payload_contains.text: The charmed stock costs more because it does more. Wear too much of it at once and it starts to argue with itself, so choose with sense. Coin on the counter, same as the rest.

payload_contains.speaker: Krshia
payload_contains.text: Guild paper and a Silverfang stone, together — the city won't ask twice. Keep both on you until the Door has done its work.
The light sharpens and the air turns to hot metal and stone dust. Pallass, tier on tier, rising past where you can see the top.

payload_contains.speaker: Tier Clerk
payload_contains.text: Stamped. Market tier, until you've got cause for more. Mind the queues.

payload_contains.speaker: Forge-Tier Clerk
payload_contains.text: Five gold, filed same-day, no exceptions and no discounts: that is the posted price. Grimalkin reads your fitness afterward, at the exam floor on the far end of this office. I only handle paper.

payload_contains.speaker: Grimalkin
payload_contains.text: Grip, cleared. Wind, cleared — barely. The last measure was whether you quit before I did. You did not. The numbers say you will survive the forge tier. The file will say 'adequate.' Ask around this office what I usually write.

payload_contains.speaker: Forge-Tier Clerk
payload_contains.text: Grimalkin's mark is on the file. Three gold for the stamp itself: posted price, same as the filing.

payload_contains.speaker: Grimalkin
payload_contains.text: I have. The forge tier runs on rune-fed work. Every ward up there eats on a schedule a smith keeps in a ledger. Two feedings a shift, logged. No smith keeps one for your door. Stand still.
The brass gate rises with a well-oiled clank, counterweights turning smooth in their track. The lift carries you up, into noise and heat and orange light.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: Three regions taught you the same word in three accents and not one of them noticed doing it. A witch feeds hers, milk and a word. An enchanter prices the draw and calls it craftsmanship. Pallass bills it as maintenance. Maintenance. Under this city is wardwork by the hand that cut our frame, and it has been drawing since before Liscor had walls. I want to read it standing in front of it.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: Good. I have walked that gauntlet twice and marked the safe line myself, so we will not be dying of a flagstone. Bring your own rope. I am not carrying yours; I have a spine to preserve and a reputation that assumes I never lift anything.
Warm air, woodsmoke, the creak of the pantry door settling shut behind you. You're back, and you didn't walk here.
Your own bed.
Your own bed.
The Door hums against the wardwork below the city. Somewhere under Liscor, something answers it now.
The light dims into torchlit stone, and the deep hush of the dungeon closes back around you. You know this quiet.
Pisces reaches the door before you do and stops a handspan short of it. "The same hand. One person's work, and this door was the first of it." He does not look away while he says it.

Pisces steps back at last. "The lines run one way. They have run one way for a very long time, and something on the far side has been drinking the whole while. Your inn has a frame by this hand. Sleep well."

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: I know. It woke the moment I said out loud what this ward has been doing, which I intend to take as a compliment. It belongs to the door, not to the dungeon: three centuries in a niche with the dust settling on it, left here against exactly one thing happening, and it has just happened. Whatever we decide about the seal, we decide it past that. Deal with it and I will hold the reading open while you do.
It is still turning toward the sound when you reach it. The first move is yours.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: We open it and see what three centuries of feeding produced. Or we leave it fed and make that somebody's paid duty, which is dull, and correct, and I resent both qualities. Or — if your hands are equal to it, which remains unproven — you re-cut the ward yourself and it holds another age without a keeper. I dislike most of these. I will be copying the outer lines while you decide.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: Then stand clear of it. The reading has to stay open while the seal comes apart, which means I am occupied and you are on your own for whatever else objects to this. The alcove was the first answer to that question. I would not assume it was the only one.
The seal does not resist. It simply stops being a seal — the runes go quiet in order, one ring at a time, and the door swings in on three centuries of undisturbed air.

Not a prisoner. An anchor: a twin to the stone the Horns hauled out of the ruin, and it has been drinking the ward's slow pour for three centuries to stay awake. Pisces, hoarse: "This is why the Door works at all. Somebody left it something to come home to, and then somebody sealed the room and let it drink."
Cut into the slab, in a hand that expected readers: a tally. Ninety-one marks, then a gap, then one more in a different chisel. Nobody came back to make the ninety-third.
Warm air, woodsmoke, the creak of the pantry door settling shut behind you. You're back, and you didn't walk here.
Your own bed.
